title: Linguistics
description: In any language the commonest word turns up about twice as often as the second, three times as often as the third: Zipf's law. Count the symbols of an unknown script and their frequencies tell you its alphabet, then its words, then its grammar; how much each symbol says is its entropy, H = log₂N for N symbols used equally. Unlocks the Decipherment Desk: the glyph tablets of the Library Ruins can be read.

puzzle.goal: A script of N symbols, each as likely as any other. Write the information H each symbol carries, in bits.
puzzle.name: Shannon's entropy of an alphabet
puzzle.ask: Find H in bits for a script of N = @{N} symbols.
puzzle.method: H = −Σ p·log₂p with every p = 1/N: N terms of (1/N)·log₂N.
